title: Dancing and stage shows in Charleston theaters
summary: He loved dancing and the movie houses with stage shows, sat in the balcony, and imitated the dancers at home.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, did you have a feel then for the beat, for something--?
Oh, well, I used to dance. I was a good dancer, more or less.
Oh, were you?
Cause my mother was a good dancer and I was always able to dance I used to.
You mean like some tap dancing? Would you, you know, do some tap dancing? Or some beats and steps?
Yeah. No, no. You know --
You just danced?
Yeah. Right. That's right.
To enjoy it. Do a little dance.
Yeah. But during that period -- later on that came--. I used to go to movies, oh, quite a bit. I loved the movies.
Yeah?
I used to live in the -- in the movies.
Yeah?
I remember when I was a kid my mother used to say when she looked for me I was always in the movies. (Laugh). That's where they had stage shows. And I loved stage shows during that period.
Yeah. Yeah.
And I remember once that Mamie Smith --
Oh? You do?
-- came to a theater there. And whenever they would have a stage show I would go.
Yeah.
Now we couldn't sit downstairs. We had to go upstairs.
Yeah.
So, I used to go up there and watch -- watch them dance. And then come home and like, imitate them. You know the dances and whatnot.
Yeah. Yeah. Well, who did you see in those days? Can you remember, I mean, do you --
No --
Guys like [Cock] and [Brown] or guys like --
Oh no, no.
I guess that was later, huh?
No, no. That's too early.
That was too early for stuff like that?
I'm talking about way back.
Yeah. Yeah.
You know, this is a long time ago.
Yeah, yeah.
You know, like I was a kid, you know.
Yeah.
